title: Shader builders, schemas and resources
summary: Build shader declarations and bind resources with schemas that agree with the uploaded data layout.

blocks.text: ShaderBuilder combines registered WGSL chunks, preprocessor flags, injection slots and schemas. ChunkRegistry resolves includes and detects missing/circular dependencies. A component can contribute helper functions and stage hooks without rewriting the whole shader. Shader compilation and pipeline validation remain runtime WebGPU operations.

VertexSchema maps shader types to vertex attributes. VaryingSchema maps inter-stage values and interpolation. UniformSchema computes fields, offsets and padded layouts; UniformBufferData writes matching CPU data. Resource declarations describe buffers, uniforms, samplers, sampled/storage textures and external video inputs. Unsupported attribute types and unknown nested uniform fields are rejected.

The current shader system separates shared view/global/state resources from geometry/fragment-specific resources. Inspect ResourceLayouts, Domains and ShaderTypes before choosing a binding index. A snippet’s group/binding numbers from a notebook may belong to an earlier layout. Reflection-driven layouts and explicit WGSL declarations must agree.

items: Start from a working geometry domain and its resource contract.
Declare vertex/varying/uniform data with matching schema types and alignment.
Inject only the stage logic needed for the effect.
Use named resources so ComputeKernel or component binding generation can resolve them.
Inspect WebGPU validation errors and compare one simple shape before adding batching or multiple views.
